rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_allow_scope.go (#5180, epic #5170): the file that defines the guard allow-overlay SCOPE ladder - repo < user < env < session - and the rule that a narrower, more-ephemeral scope layers on top and therefore wins.
rows.distinction: The scope PRECEDENCE table, not a storage location: it ranks the overlay layers - NOT guardAllowOverlayPaths (which enumerates the ordered read PATHS) and NOT guard_policy.go (the `fak guard policy` verb router).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_allow_scope.go: maps a scope name to its integer precedence rank - higher rank = narrower and more ephemeral = layered on top; an unknown scope ranks below everything so it can never claim to shadow a known scope.
rows.distinction: The ORDERING function over scopes - NOT guardAllowScopeSession (the string constant naming one scope) and NOT guardAllowScopeDurabilityNote (the prose legend about how long a scope's widening lives).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_allow_scope.go: the string constant "session" naming the session-scope overlay layer; the repo/user/env layer names come from guardAllowOverlayPaths, so this is the one scope name that needs its own constant.
rows.distinction: The NAME of the narrowest scope - NOT guardAllowScopeRank (its position in the precedence order) and NOT guardAllowLayersWithSessionScope (the function that appends the layer).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_allow_scope.go: returns the one-clause operator legend saying whether a widening recorded at a given scope survives the next launch, so every scope listing answers the durability question without the reader inferring it from a path.
rows.distinction: The human-readable DURABILITY sentence for a scope - NOT guardAllowScopeRank (its numeric precedence) and NOT the overlay file the widening is stored in.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_allow_scope.go: appends the session-scope layer AFTER the base overlay layers, leaving the base order untouched, so the session scope is applied last and therefore takes precedence.
rows.distinction: The function that ADDS the session layer to a layer list - NOT guardAllowOverlayPaths (which builds the base layers) and NOT guardAllowScopeSession (the scope's name constant).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_allow_scope.go: the environment variable (constant guardAllowSessionIDEnv) that carries the guard session id to a process that did not resolve it itself, so operator tooling beside a guarded session can address that session's scope.
rows.distinction: The env var that TRANSPORTS an already-resolved guard session id - NOT FAK_GUARD_ALLOW_OVERLAY (which names an overlay file) and NOT maybeRecordGuardSessionIndex (which publishes a session into the fleet index).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_stops.go: the environment variable whose VALUE is the absolute stops-ledger path the guard installer injects into the Stop hook child; unset means recording is disabled entirely.
rows.distinction: The env var NAME as it appears in the environment - NOT guardStopsLedgerEnv (the Go constant that holds this string) and NOT the ledger file itself.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_stops.go: the Go constant that holds the string "FAK_GUARD_STOPS_LEDGER" - the single in-code spelling of the stops-ledger env var, so the installer and the Stop hook can never disagree about the name.
rows.distinction: The identifier in Go source - NOT the FAK_GUARD_STOPS_LEDGER environment variable it names, and NOT guardToolprocJournalRel (a relative journal PATH constant, not an env var name).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/commit_msg_advisory.go: the gate-mode env var for the commit-message advisory; it can only SILENCE the advisory (`off`), never escalate it to a refusal.
rows.distinction: A SILENCE-only advisory knob - NOT a refusing guard gate, and NOT FLEET_ALLOW_MSG (the paired escape variable read beside it).

rows.definition: internal/policy/amendment.go: the AmendmentClass constant for operator-gated LOOSENING of a policy knob (allow overlay, reload-widen) - the class that may move a knob outward, but only through an operator gate.
rows.distinction: One of the three amendment CLASSES (beside FROZEN and RATCHET), so it describes what an amendment is allowed to do - NOT guardAllowScopeRank (where a widening is recorded) and NOT the allow-overlay file that records one.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_codex_oauth.go: the constant base URL of the ChatGPT backend Codex API the guard's Codex OAuth path talks to.
rows.distinction: A remote HTTP endpoint constant - NOT guardToolprocJournalRel (a workspace-relative file path) and NOT an env var an operator sets.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_toolproc_hooks.go: the workspace-relative journal path (.fak/toolproc/journal.jsonl) the toolproc hooks append to - one shared journal per workspace, made absolute at install so the hook is cwd-independent.
rows.distinction: The TOOL-PROCESS journal every guarded session in a workspace shares - NOT the stops ledger (FAK_GUARD_STOPS_LEDGER, a per-install path) and NOT the negframe journal the reframe telemetry writes.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_support.go: reports whether the guard's own STDIN is a real console, using term.IsTerminal rather than an os.ModeCharDevice test - because on Windows a redirected stdin reports AS a character device and a FileMode check would read the headless case as interactive.
rows.distinction: A probe of the STDIN handle only, used so an attended user is never blocked - NOT guardOwnsInteractiveTerminal, which asks the different question of whether this process owns a terminal HOST it may launch a window in.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_resolve.go: reports whether this guard owns an interactive terminal host it may act in - false for any dispatcher-owned session (FAK_DISPATCH_ID, FAK_HEADLESS, CI), then per-OS on WT_SESSION / TERM_PROGRAM / TERM+SSH_TTY.
rows.distinction: An OWNERSHIP question about the terminal host, guarding the double-launch of a dispatcher-owned session - NOT cmdGuardStdinInteractive, which only asks whether the STDIN handle is a console.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/info_panels.go: renders the agent cell of one `fak info` guard-session row; it deliberately does NOT render Recontinue as sub-agent depth, because Recontinue is the same agent after a budget-reset re-continuation, not a spawned child.
rows.distinction: A per-row RENDERER for the info panel - NOT the guard-session index row it reads, and NOT SpawnCount (the parent-side sub-agent count rendered beside it).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_negframe_summary.go: records the SessionStart negframe row and TRUNCATES the journal first, because SessionStart is the session boundary - without the reset the exit summary would report a lifetime total under a per-session label.
rows.distinction: The journal RESET-and-open call at session start - NOT guardNegframeReframe (the per-emit reframe) and NOT guardNegframeSummary (the exit-time fold).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_negframe_summary.go: the single gated seam that reframes fak-authored fragments at emit time - on the treatment arm it reframes and reports that pass's telemetry, on the control arm it concatenates the fragments unreframed; non-fak-authored fragments survive byte-for-byte on both arms.
rows.distinction: The A/B-gated TRANSFORM applied to outgoing text - NOT guardNegframeBegin (which opens the journal) and NOT negframe.ReframeFakOnly, which it wraps so no caller reaches the transform ungated.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_negframe_summary.go: folds the workspace negframe journal that the SessionStart reframe feeds into the one-line guard exit summary.
rows.distinction: The EXIT-time reader of the journal - NOT guardNegframeReframe (the emit-time writer) and NOT RenderNegframePane (the scorecard pane rendered elsewhere).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_sessions.go: the precondition wrapper around recordGuardSessionIndex - it returns "" without touching the index when there is no audit journal, no command or no trace id, so a launch with nothing to publish never appends a partial row.
rows.distinction: The GUARD in front of the index append, not the append itself - NOT recordGuardSessionIndex (which does the write) and NOT recordGuardUsage (which appends a usage row at exit).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/usagelog_record.go: appends the single best-effort usage row for a `fak guard` invocation at exit, once (sync.Once) and only when a start time was stamped; any failure is swallowed so meta-observability can never change the verb's outcome.
rows.distinction: The EXIT-time usage-log append for the guard verb - NOT maybeRecordGuardSessionIndex (the START-time session-index publish) and NOT the stops ledger.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_policy.go (#5424, epic #5170): the router for `fak guard policy <verb>` - it holds the verb table and dispatches to the explain / diff implementations that live in their own files.
rows.distinction: The CLI verb ROUTER for policy inspection - NOT internal/policy (the amendment-class model it reports on) and NOT guard_allow_scope.go (the overlay scope ladder).

rows.definition: internal/mcpfootprint/floorgate.go (#2924): the one-way ratchet on fak's always-sent MCP tool-schema floor - it refuses GROWTH past FloorBudgetTokens (FLOOR_BUDGET_EXCEEDED) and also refuses SLACK once a deferral lever has driven the floor well below the ceiling (FLOOR_BUDGET_STALE), so the budget must be re-pinned.
rows.distinction: The REFUSAL half of the tool-footprint work, denominated in ESTIMATED tokens - NOT Price()/PerToolSorted() (the measurement half) and NOT a provider-billed count it must never be compared against.

rows.definition: internal/model/arch.go: runs one layer's f32 gated MLP over N already-post-normed rows and returns the [N,H] down projection - gate/up matMulBatch, then fuseGatedMLPPanels, then down.
rows.distinction: "Gated" here is FFN GATING (SwiGLU-style gate/up), not a policy gate: this is a compute path - NOT floorgate (a refusal gate) and NOT fuseGatedMLPPanels (the in-place panel step it calls).

rows.definition: internal/model/arch.go: finishes a batched gated MLP's gate and up panels IN PLACE - the single source of truth for that mechanical axis, so every prefill/quant/batch twin applies it identically.
rows.distinction: The in-place PANEL step, one axis of the FFN - NOT batchedGatedMLP (the whole gate/up/down layer that calls it) and NOT a policy gate.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/growthgate.go: appends one JSON line per growth-gate reap decision - the accountability trail for BOTH a dry run and an --apply run, mirroring the fleet-janitor ledger.
rows.distinction: The LEDGER WRITER for reap decisions - NOT growthReapDecision (the record it writes) and NOT the growth gate's refusal itself.

rows.definition: internal/gateway/session_ceiling.go (constant envMaxSessions): the operator-configured ceiling on CONCURRENT governed sessions; 0 or unset means unbounded.
rows.distinction: The operator's ceiling INPUT - NOT SESSION_CEILING_SATURATED (the refusal reason emitted when the ceiling is reached) and NOT the fak_sessions gauge (the live count it is compared against).

rows.definition: internal/gateway/session_ceiling.go: the closed-vocabulary refusal reason a new-session admission carries when the live governed-session count is at or over the configured ceiling; declared in dos.toml so dos_check_reason resolves it.
rows.distinction: A REASON code returned on refusal - NOT FAK_MAX_SESSIONS (the ceiling that produced it) and NOT the fak_sessions gauge (the live count).

rows.definition: internal/gateway/metrics_render.go: the Prometheus gauge fak_sessions{state} - a READ-TIME fold of the session registry into live served sessions per DRIVE run-state token, so a GC'd session decrements its bucket on the next scrape.
rows.distinction: A per-run-state gauge of LIVE served sessions - NOT the governed-session count measured against the ceiling, NOT FAK_MAX_SESSIONS (the ceiling itself), and NOT FAK_SESSION_ID, which is one session's identity rather than a population count.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/session_query.go (#3461): the SECOND process's side of the guard-session contract - it discovers a running `fak guard` through the guard-session index and performs a read-scoped raw status read against the address and bearer it published.
rows.distinction: The READER side of the guard-session index - NOT maybeRecordGuardSessionIndex (the publishing side) and NOT internal/guardsessions (the index storage package).

rows.definition: internal/sessionaudit: the field carrying ONE representative session id for an aggregated audit finding, so an operator reading a count can open a concrete session that exhibits it.
rows.distinction: A single EXEMPLAR id attached to an aggregate - NOT StuckSessions or SilentConfusedSessions (the counts it exemplifies) and NOT a session-id format.

rows.definition: internal/gateway/ctxrestore.go: the ceiling on the per-session context-restore stash table; on overflow the whole table takes a generational reset, so a gateway minting a fresh trace per session cannot grow it without limit.
rows.distinction: A bound on the ctx-RESTORE stash (tombstones for a dropped first user turn) - NOT maxCtxValueSessions (the sibling bound on the ctx-VALUE table it mirrors) and NOT FAK_MAX_SESSIONS (an admission ceiling, not a table size).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/serve_stages.go: the `fak serve` startup stage that resolves auth/key material, validates the budget flags, cold-resumes persisted session drive state (#629), and seeds the default trace's budget and durability registration.
rows.distinction: The SESSION plane of serve startup - NOT buildGateway (the later stage that constructs the gateway server and arms admission) and NOT the session registry it seeds.

rows.definition: internal/leaseref/session.go: the basename prefix "session-" that marks a session DESCRIPTOR ref apart from a lock lease inside the shared refs/fak/locks/ namespace; the stored id omits it, so a caller addresses a session by its plain id.
rows.distinction: A git-ref NAMESPACE marker for lease refs - NOT SessionPrefixIndex (a warm prompt-prefix map in the gateway); the two share the word "prefix" and mean entirely different things.

rows.definition: internal/gateway/session_prefix_index.go: maps a platform-agnostic session-prefix key to the warm PROMPT prefix a conversation established, so a channel hop reuses that prefix instead of cold-re-sending the transcript; Establish keeps the first channel as home and Resume prices the cache_read the reuse served.
rows.distinction: A warm PROMPT-prefix reuse index across channels - NOT sessionPrefix (a git-ref basename marker) and NOT the KV cache itself.

rows.canonical: SessionThroughput (wire form of the throughput budget)
rows.definition: internal/gateway/gateway.go: the WIRE form of internal/session.ThroughputBudget (#2762) - the soft pace-shaping rate plus the enforced minimum sustained-rate floor; ObservedTokensPerSec is a read-only projection and is ignored on control writes.
rows.distinction: The transport-facing DTO for a session's configured rates - NOT session.ThroughputBudget (the internal type it mirrors) and NOT the observed rate field it carries read-only.

rows.canonical: SilentConfusedSessions (confusion invisible to the tool lens)
rows.definition: internal/sessionaudit: counts confused sessions the tool-I/O Behavior lens was BLIND to (behaviorSessionStuck == false) - prose thrash while every tool call succeeded. It is the slice that justifies the prose lens and the primary gate for the confusion_pressure recommendation.
rows.distinction: The subset of confusion NO tool-failure signal can see - NOT StuckSessions (the behaviour-lens stuck count) and NOT a total of all confused sessions.

rows.definition: internal/sessionaudit: the count of sessions the tool-I/O Behavior lens judged STUCK, carried through the audit feed and the compact projection.
rows.distinction: The count the BEHAVIOUR lens can see - NOT SilentConfusedSessions (precisely the cases that lens is blind to) and NOT ExampleSession (one exemplar id).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/wip.go: recovers a WIP record's session id from its stamp, falling back to the ref name - the same identity rule the pure fold uses, so the census and the ticket path agree on who owns a checkpoint.
rows.distinction: The IDENTITY rule for a WIP checkpoint's owner - NOT DISCARD_WITNESSED (a reconciliation verdict about that checkpoint) and NOT the ref itself.

rows.definition: internal/gatewayusageledger/compaction_segments.go: the subset of compaction Bails whose reason means the request was never a compaction CANDIDATE. Reported rather than silently subtracted, and derived from the reason map - a row with a bail COUNT but no reasons contributes 0 here and stays in the candidate denominator.
rows.distinction: The population HELD OUT of the candidate rate - NOT candidateBails (the eligible population) and NOT CandidateBailRate (the ratio computed from both).

rows.definition: internal/gateway/metrics_observe.go: the half of compactBailPartition's split that WAS a compaction candidate. An unrecognised reason counts here (fail-open), so a reason added upstream without registration leaves the measured rate conservatively high instead of silently shrinking the population.
rows.distinction: The ELIGIBLE bail population - NOT NonCandidateBails (its complement) and NOT the raw attempts{bailed} counter that mixes both.

rows.definition: internal/gatewayusageledger/compaction_segments.go: the ledger field (Bails-NonCandidateBails)/(Fires + Bails-NonCandidateBails) - declines over ELIGIBLE attempts, 0 when the eligible population is empty. It is the health read BailRate cannot carry (#5388), and BailRate is kept beside it unchanged for continuity.
rows.distinction: The SEGMENTED-LEDGER field - NOT compactCandidateBailRate (the live gateway computation of the same ratio) and NOT BailRate (the raw ratio over all attempts).

rows.definition: internal/gateway/metrics_observe.go: computes fires/(fires+candidateBails) at observe time, returning an honest zero when the eligible population is empty rather than a fabricated ratio (#5443/#5388).
rows.distinction: The live GATEWAY-side function - NOT CandidateBailRate (the persisted ledger field it feeds) and NOT the raw bail rate, which the unchanged attempts{bailed} counter still makes recoverable.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/route_place.go: builds the candidate pool a rung placement draws from, excluding compatibility-only and deprecated-alias bindings (legacy spellings of a model already in the pool) and admitting a model with no declared capability UNMEASURED at the strictest tier.
rows.distinction: The UNGRADED admission pool - NOT gradedPool (the same pool after evidence grading) and NOT GradeCandidates (the grader that produces those grades).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/dispatch_price.go: projects any candidate slice onto the plain string slice the shared wave/lane helpers take, with the key accessor supplied by the caller because the price and wave candidate types name their identity differently (Name vs ID).
rows.distinction: A generic KEY PROJECTION over candidates - NOT placementCandidates (which builds a model pool) and NOT the wave/lane helpers it feeds.

rows.definition: internal/modelroute/capability.go: grades EVERY model in a fixed order so a placement built from evidence is as reproducible as one built from a hand-written declaration; a model with no evidence still appears, ungraded and therefore top-rung only.
rows.distinction: The plural, order-fixed grader over a model LIST - NOT GradeCapability (the single-model fold it calls) and NOT gradedPool (the candidate pool the grades are then applied to).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_support.go: the side-effect-free decision of WHETHER to enable the guard audit journal, at what path, and whether that path was SYNTHESIZED from the repo-local default - so the precedence (boot env, then --no-audit/--audit off, then --audit PATH, then repo default) is unit-testable without touching the global journal.
rows.distinction: A pure PLANNING function whose output the caller acts on - NOT guardEnableAudit (which performs the enable) and NOT the journal file itself; the isDefault bit is what lets a failed default-on enable degrade to a warning.

rows.definition: internal/gateway/gateway.go: picks the chat backend for the /v1/chat/completions and /v1/messages surfaces from the wired configuration - a dual local-alongside-API planner, a proxy planner, the in-kernel chat planner, or the deterministic mock - and records the planner-init startup phase.
rows.distinction: The BACKEND CHOOSER for the chat surfaces, so "planner" here means a serving backend - NOT a work planner that produces a plan document.

rows.definition: internal/quality/suite_corpus.go: the planned shape of a quality suite run over its corpus - what suite_split.go then splits into the executed parts.
rows.distinction: A CORPUS/split plan for a quality suite - NOT selectChatPlanner (which selects a serving backend) and NOT a dispatch launch plan.

rows.definition: internal/gateway/residency_router.go: forms TWO choices per request - the LOCALITY target (longest resident prefix overlap) and the BALANCE target (least-loaded worker) - and routes to whichever wins prefix-overlap-length x inverse-load; past SkewThreshold it drops locality entirely and routes by load alone.
rows.distinction: A ROUTING policy that uses cache residency as a score - NOT a cache eviction or admission policy, and NOT PrefixResidencyIndex (the index it reads and self-populates).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_preflight.go: the timed form of the dispatch preflight - it returns the preflight map PLUS a per-stage millisecond timing map (process_snapshot, kernel_probe, ...); dispatchPreflight is the thin wrapper that drops the timings.
rows.distinction: The variant that also reports WHERE the preflight time went - NOT dispatchPreflight (the untimed wrapper) and NOT PreflightRefuseNoAccount (one of the refusal reasons the preflight can produce).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_preflight.go: the file holding the dispatch tick's admission preflight - the host process snapshot, the kernel probe, the seat pool read and the published per-worker load (OSWorkerProcs) that together decide how many workers a tick may admit.
rows.distinction: The ADMISSION-CAPACITY preflight run before a tick dispatches - NOT the guard's per-tool adjudication and NOT dispatch_tick_load_debounce.go (the load publisher it reads from).

rows.definition: internal/modelroute/capability.go: folds ONE model's observed outcomes into a capability grade, deterministically in the evidence - rows are merged per class before anything is compared, so the same rows in any order yield the same grade.
rows.distinction: The SINGLE-model grader - NOT GradeCandidates (the fixed-order grader over a list of models) and NOT gradedPool (the pool the resulting grades are applied to).

rows.definition: internal/dispatchtick/witness.go: the no-commit CAUSE constant "policy_block" - the witness classification for a worker that produced no commit because policy refused it, as distinct from a worker that simply did nothing.
rows.distinction: A no-commit CLASSIFICATION recorded by the witness - NOT the policy refusal itself, and NOT PreflightRefuseNoAccount (a pre-launch refusal reason, before any worker ran).

rows.definition: internal/dispatchtick/preflight.go: the preflight refusal constant "REFUSE_NO_ACCOUNT" - a dispatch is refused before launch because no seat/account is available to run it.
rows.distinction: A PRE-LAUNCH refusal reason - NOT NoCommitPolicyBlock (a POST-run witness cause) and NOT the preflight capacity numbers themselves.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/dispatch_model_policy.go: resolves which model a dispatched worker runs under, through a fixed precedence - operator pin, bench gate, per-issue tier profile, then the work-class model default - and builds the downgrade chain with the primary dropped so a Layer-2 switch never re-dispatches onto the walled model.
rows.distinction: The PRECEDENCE resolver for a worker's model - NOT GradeCapability (which measures what a model can do) and NOT the fallback chain it emits.

rows.definition: internal/metrics/cache_break.go (#2916): the observability half of the cache-integrity invariant - a first-class runtime counter of how often the prompt prefix actually broke and what each break cost, under a CLOSED cause label, so a cache regression is caught by a gate rather than by the invoice.
rows.distinction: The WITNESS surface for prefix breaks - NOT the prefix-mutation detector that reports a break, and NOT the cache-value pricing ledger.

rows.definition: internal/metrics/cache_break.go: the CLOSED vocabulary for why a cached prompt prefix broke; a closed set (rather than free text) is what lets a regression gate reason by cause, and anything outside it folds to CacheBreakUnknown.
rows.distinction: The CAUSE label, not the event: it says WHY a prefix broke - NOT CacheBreakEvent (one witnessed break, cause plus cost) and NOT CacheBreakReport (the folded readout).

rows.definition: internal/metrics/cache_break.go: folds a session's cache-break witnesses into the CacheBreakReport, enumerating causes in a canonical deterministic order so the witnessed output is stable across runs.
rows.distinction: The READ-side fold from events to a report - NOT recordCacheBreak / WitnessCacheBreak (the write side that appends one event) and NOT CacheBreakCause (the label it groups by).

rows.definition: internal/gateway/metrics_observe.go: the gateway-side CONSUMER seam that witnesses one cache-break event - the caller supplies cause and cold-rebuild token cost, internal/metrics normalizes them, a nil metrics is a no-op, and the append is off the hot path under its own lock.
rows.distinction: The WRITE seam a gateway calls per break - NOT FoldCacheBreaks (the read-time fold) and NOT the prefix-mutation detector that decides a break happened.

rows.definition: internal/gateway/metrics_render.go: the counter of cache_control BREAKPOINT PLACEMENT attempts on the outbound body, labelled by outcome (placed, or the refusal reason).
rows.distinction: Counts attempts to PLACE a cache breakpoint - NOT the cache-break counters, which count an established prefix BREAKING; placement is a write-side decision, a break is an observed loss.

rows.definition: internal/gateway/metrics_render.go: the gauge of NET realized provider-cache saving in input-token-equivalents (baseline minus actual). It is NEGATIVE on a cold-write-dominated session until reads repay the writes, and is the same engine and number as `fak vcache observe`.
rows.distinction: A NET, signed saving that can legitimately read negative - NOT VCacheTokenEquiv (the unit conversion it is denominated in) and NOT a gross cache-read count.

rows.definition: internal/cachevaluereport/fleet_benefit.go: selects the savings buckets that carry compaction-lever telemetry - the fak-authored rows plus any mechanism in the compaction family - so the terminal and markdown renderers fold the fire/starve/shed trend from exactly the same rows; nil means no lever-health section.
rows.distinction: A ROW SELECTOR over savings buckets - NOT compaction_segments.go (which segments by budget regime and session length) and NOT the lever itself.

rows.definition: internal/gatewayusageledger/compaction_segments.go: the compaction-effectiveness fold SEGMENTED by budget regime x session-length band - it exists because the fleet's compaction-shed numbers are only comparable WITHIN a budget regime (the 48000 interactive default versus the headless one).
rows.distinction: A SEGMENTED fold whose whole point is refusing to average across regimes - NOT compactionLeverBuckets (a bucket filter) and NOT the raw ledger rows.

rows.canonical: CompactionSolvencyForced (fires forced by the solvency floor)
rows.definition: internal/gateway/metrics.go: the count of fires the head-anchored burst economics REFUSED and the context-solvency floor forced anyway - a SUBSET of CompactionFired, broken out because an ordinary fire repays in cache dollars while a forced one is knowingly taken at a loss to keep the session inside its context window.
rows.distinction: The knowingly-uneconomic SUBSET of fires, which the cache-value ledger must not book as savings - NOT CompactionFired (the total) and NOT a fault count; a forced fire is the override working.

rows.canonical: formatCompactionBudgetNudge (budget line for the debug pane)
rows.definition: internal/gateway/debug_stats.go: renders the ' budget=spent:... ctx:.../...' nudge line from prompt/completion/cache-read/cache-create against the compaction budget; empty when no budget is set or nothing is resident.
rows.distinction: A RENDERER of the residency-versus-budget line - NOT compactionBudgetPast (the boolean predicate beside it that decides whether the budget is exceeded) and NOT the compactor's own fire decision.

rows.definition: internal/rsiloop/firenettune.go: the PURE fold that prices ONE fire's OBSERVED facts into a scored receipt on the canonical cacheprice basis (#2798) - the same economics CacheBurstBreakEvenTurns prices ex-ante.
rows.distinction: The EX-POST scoring of a fire that already happened - NOT CacheBurstBreakEvenTurns (the ex-ante estimate on the same basis) and NOT CompactionSolvencyForced (a count of overridden fires).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/commit_msg_advisory.go: prints the commit-message advisory by RE-LINTING the final message rather than reusing the pre-derivation report, so a subject the derivation healed produces no warning; exempt subject classes (a release anchor, a merge/revert, a bookkeeping snapshot) are honoured and never nagged.
rows.distinction: An ADVISORY renderer that describes what will actually land - NOT the commit-message linter it calls, and NOT a refusal: FLEET_MSG_GUARD can only silence it.

rows.definition: internal/issuefanout/coverage.go: prints the issue-fan-out coverage scorecard for a human - the two headline rates, one evidence row per new leaf, and the named offenders behind each rate.
rows.distinction: The PRINTER for a CoverageReport - NOT Coverage() (the fold that computes it) and NOT coverageReport in cmd/fak/route_coverage.go, which renders MODEL-ROUTE coverage and merely shares the word.

rows.definition: internal/metrics/device_spine_tui.go: renders the fleet overview grid - one fixed-height card per device, column-wrapped to the given width, in the view's stable first-seen order, over the SAME snapshot slice every other renderer reads.
rows.distinction: A TUI GRID over device metrics - NOT RenderReceipt (a per-field receipt view) and NOT a metrics collection path; it adds no new collection.

rows.definition: internal/agent/receipt.go: writes the human, per-field-labeled receipt view of an agent Receipt plus the verification verdict (a nil verifyErr means it verified against the journal).
rows.distinction: A per-RECEIPT human view that also states whether the receipt verified - NOT RenderOverview (a device grid) and NOT the journal it is verified against.

rows.definition: internal/gateway/refusal_notes.go: folds every registered note renderer over ONE refused adjudication and returns the space-joined actionable notes plus whether any of them was a preview-confirm recipe; both content-channel call sites consume this instead of stitching notes by hand.
rows.distinction: The single FOLD over refusal-note renderers - NOT an individual note renderer, and NOT the adjudication decision it explains.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/superloop.go: reads each super-loop member's status from the cheap committed surfaces off the hot path - scorecard debt from the pinned control-pane baseline, loop liveness from the cross-ledger loop-health fold - descending a sub-super-loop inline while garden/surface members stay descend pointers.
rows.distinction: The ENTRY POINT for one walk - NOT superloopCollector (the once-per-walk cache of those surfaces it constructs) and NOT runSuperloopDrive (which admits and may run a member).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/superloop.go: holds the cheap committed surfaces read ONCE per walk (the pinned scorecard baseline, the cross-ledger loop-health fold, the trajectory ledger), so a recursive descent through sub-super-loops re-reads nothing; its descend() refuses an unknown ref or a cycle as UNMEASURED.
rows.distinction: The per-walk STATE that makes the recursive descent cheap and cycle-safe - NOT collectSuperloopStatuses (the function that creates and drives it).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/superloop_drive.go: the `fak superloop drive` entry point - it admits up to --batch worst-first members whose regions are mutually disjoint (and disjoint from live leases) through the lease-admission gate, optionally executing each admitted member's own front door behind the held lease.
rows.distinction: The ADMIT-and-optionally-RUN verb - NOT collectSuperloopStatuses (the read-only status walk it decides from) and NOT the loop ledger it records its admission witness to.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/dojo.go: tolerantly reads the workspace's ACTIVE loop-ledger segment; a missing ledger or a chain break degrades to the recovered prefix, so the dispatch-yield episode reports itself UNMEASURED instead of failing the run.
rows.distinction: A TOLERANT reader that degrades rather than errors - NOT recordDispatchTickLoop (the writer that appends a tick row) and NOT the ledger file itself.

rows.canonical: recordDispatchTickLoop (tick row into the loop ledger)
rows.definition: cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_worker.go: appends one dispatch-tick row to the loop ledger - deriving the run id and loop id from the payload and recording the tick's live flag, lane issue count, step budget, worker cap and preflight live/cap numbers.
rows.distinction: The WRITER of a dispatch-tick loop row - NOT loadLoopLedgerEvents (the tolerant reader) and NOT the dispatch preflight whose numbers it copies.

rows.definition: internal/model/arch_support.go: the surface stating which checkpoint architectures fak's in-kernel forward actually implements - it carries the forward-path classification and the typed refusal for anything it does not.
rows.distinction: The SUPPORT/refusal surface for an architecture - NOT the per-architecture forward code itself, and NOT the GGUF loader's arch metadata read.

rows.definition: internal/model/arch_support.go: the typed refusal newModel returns when a checkpoint carries weights for an architecture whose in-kernel forward fak does not yet implement, so `fak serve` can surface a named refusal before serving a token instead of binding the gateway and panicking on the first turn.
rows.distinction: A LOAD-TIME typed refusal about the architecture - NOT a runtime forward error and NOT arch_support.go (the file that classifies support).

rows.definition: CoverageReport is a REUSED name, not one type: internal/accountprobe grades an enrolled seat roster (and separately reports whether the ledger said anything at all); internal/issuefanout is the two-rate adoption scorecard with per-leaf evidence; internal/productscorecard.CoverageReport is a FUNCTION over a catalog; and cmd/fak/route_coverage.go's lowercase coverageReport renders model-route coverage.
rows.distinction: A name a reader must disambiguate BY PACKAGE before trusting it - NOT one type; in particular the accountprobe and issuefanout reports measure entirely different populations (seats versus new leaves).

rows.definition: internal/issuefanout/coverage.go: the default cap on issues scanned when measuring fan-out coverage (20000). It is deliberately NOT the dedupe bound - fan-out markers cluster in OLDER issues, so a small window returns zero markers and reports a confident 0% that is simply wrong; a scan that hits the cap is marked truncated and forces OK false.
rows.distinction: A SCAN-WINDOW bound whose exhaustion is reported as NOT PROVEN - NOT the dedupe bound it was deliberately split from, and NOT a coverage rate.

rows.definition: internal/issuefanout/coverage.go: ONE leaf's evidence row inside the fan-out coverage scorecard - the per-leaf witness behind the headline rates.
rows.distinction: A per-leaf EVIDENCE ROW - NOT internal/wiki's leaf_coverage float (a wiki score field that shares the name) and NOT CoverageReport (the whole scorecard).

rows.definition: internal/model/config.go: the config field that OVERRIDES the per-head attention scale denominator - when non-zero (Gemma) the scale is 1/sqrt(QueryPreAttnScalar) instead of 1/sqrt(HeadDim), which is why Gemma 27B's 144 differs from its head dim.
rows.distinction: The DENOMINATOR OVERRIDE, a config input - NOT attnScale (the computed SDPA denominator it feeds) and NOT longropeAttnScaleMul (a multiplicative Phi-longrope adjustment applied to the same scale).

rows.definition: internal/model/longrope.go: the multiplicative attention-scale adjustment the Phi longrope path applies on top of the 1/sqrt(denominator) term.
rows.distinction: A MULTIPLIER on the attention scale, driven by the rope configuration - NOT QueryPreAttnScalar (which replaces the denominator) and NOT attnScale itself.

rows.definition: internal/model: the FALCON-family checkpoint tensor namespace - self_attention.query_key_value.weight (a fused QKV panel split at materialize time) and self_attention.dense, which fak canonicalizes to self_attn.o_proj.
rows.distinction: The Falcon-export SPELLING, which fak aliases away at load - NOT self_attn (fak's canonical projection namespace) and NOT a runtime attention kernel.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/growthgate.go: one reap outcome record - what a dry run WOULD delete, or what an --apply run reaped or failed to reap; the JSON-tagged accountability record the reap ledger is made of.
rows.distinction: A per-item REAP RECORD covering both dry-run and apply - NOT RestartDecision (a process-restart verdict) and NOT appendGrowthgateReapLedger (the writer that serialises it).

rows.definition: internal/loopmgr/restart.go: the structured verdict returned by RestartPolicy.Decide - Restart means a restart is still allowed and is scheduled for RestartAtUnixNano; GiveUp means the caller must stop restarting and surface Reason. Re-deciding inside the backoff window returns the SAME time, so duplicate watchdog ticks debounce instead of spawning a second process.
rows.distinction: A RESTART-or-GIVE-UP verdict about a supervised process - NOT TrajectoryWatchdogDecision (which decides how to INTERVENE in a live agent session) and NOT growthReapDecision (a deletion record).

rows.definition: internal/resume/trajectory_watchdog.go: the clock- and IO-free intervention verdict for a watched agent session. Liveness dominates: a dead session revives from the independently-read fresh anchor; a living healthy or slow session is untouched; a living STALL gets the cheapest reversible nudge first and only escalates after that nudge was tried.
rows.distinction: An INTERVENTION choice for a live agent trajectory - NOT RestartDecision (a process-restart schedule) and NOT the soft diagnostic dump the SoftWatchdog captures beside it, which never alters this decision.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/serve_stages.go: the `fak serve` startup stage that loads the optional model-routing policy, constructs the gateway server from the already-resolved planes, and arms the admission controller for a pure in-kernel serve.
rows.distinction: The CONSTRUCTION stage of serve startup - NOT resolveSessionPlane (the earlier stage that resolves auth, budgets and session drive state it consumes) and NOT the gateway type itself.

rows.definition: internal/gateway/metrics_render.go: the cumulative count of COLD tool DEFINITIONS marked defer_loading:true on the outbound Anthropic body across a session - the 10x floor lever (--defer-cold-tools, #3232). It is cache-safe by construction (deterministic, byte-stable tools[] turn over turn), and the provider-side context drop it drives is OBSERVED via input_tokens/cache_read, never claimed by this counter.
rows.distinction: Counts DEFINITIONS deferred, not turns and not tokens saved - NOT fak_gateway_tool_defer_standdown_turns_total (its denominator: turns where the transform ran and stood down) and NOT floorgate (the budget that refuses growth).

rows.definition: internal/wiprecon/recon.go: the reconciliation ACTION for a crashed owner's checkpoint whose delta already LANDED in HEAD (git-witnessed), so dropping it loses nothing. Fail-safe by construction: the only path to it requires Landed==true.
rows.distinction: The one action justified by a GIT WITNESS that the work is already in HEAD - NOT RECLAIM or QUARANTINE (the actions for deltas that did NOT land) and NOT wipSessionOf (which only identifies the owner).

rows.definition: validWitness is a REUSED name for two different membership tests: internal/dsparity's map of accepted parity Witness values, and internal/trajctl's function over a WitnessRung. Both answer 'is this witness value in the closed set', over unrelated vocabularies.
rows.distinction: A per-package VOCABULARY check, not one shared validator - NOT a claim that a witness is TRUE of the tree; it only says the value is a known member.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_witness.go: audits the workers that have EXITED, bucketing each resolve log into witnessed / unwitnessed / no-commit claims and returning the per-worker witness records.
rows.distinction: A POST-EXIT audit of what a worker actually committed - NOT NoCommitPolicyBlock (one of the no-commit causes it can record) and NOT validWitness (a vocabulary membership test).

rows.definition: internal/radixkv/eviction_strategy.go: the tree's CURRENT victim rule accessor - it defaults an unset tree (a bare New()) to pure LRU so the zero value keeps its historical behaviour.
rows.distinction: The rule that chooses WHICH resident block to drop - NOT CacheAwarePolicy (a routing policy that reads residency) and NOT the retention request that asks for space.

rows.definition: internal/ggufload/gguf_tensor_canonical.go: the allow-list predicate for architectures whose GGUF q/k weights are stored in the HF rotary layout and must be consumed exactly as stored - running those through unpermuteRotaryTensor would scramble every head's rotary pairs. Anything off the list keeps the historical unpermute.
rows.distinction: A per-architecture LAYOUT question about how q/k weights are STORED - NOT the rotary computation itself, and NOT UnsupportedArchError (whether the arch is implemented at all).

rows.definition: cmd/fak/route_place_evidence.go: applies capability grades to a candidate pool. A grade that did not reach the bar leaves its candidate exactly as it was - ungraded and therefore top-rung only - because failing to MEASURE something is not evidence against it; a model claimed by both a hand declaration and evidence is refused by the caller before this runs.
rows.distinction: The pool AFTER evidence grading - NOT placementCandidates (the ungraded admission pool it starts from) and NOT GradeCandidates (the grader that produced the grades).
